geometry_notes: Building height in walls.json (14.8 m) is the clerestory penthouse; the main roof of spine and wing is 11.6-11.8 m (lidar), the pavilion 5.0 m, the link 3.3 m, the east annexes 2.8-4.3 m, the east block 11.9-12.8 m with a 15.3 m box at W18 s 0-10.

Clerestory penthouse on the spine roof: ~31 m x 8 m, top 14.8 m, along the spine centre from about art (1073.9,200.5)/(1081.5,204.4) at its north end to (1089.3,170.2)/(1096.9,174.1) at its south end (lidar s 60-91 along W1, 6.5-15 m in from W1). Long sides are continuous clerestory ribbons of white-framed windows (~1.3 m tall, ~1.2 m mullion pitch); the short ends are brick (brick_buff_sun). A grey steel stair with railings climbs from the main roof to the penthouse roof along its east side near the south end.

Observatory dome 1 (the big one) sits on the penthouse roof near its south end: centre art (1090.8,177.2), white hemisphere ~4 m diameter on a short white drum, top 19.8 m (lidar), with the shutter slot.

Observatory dome 2 (small) sits on the main roof near the south end: centre art (1101.9,159.8), white, ~3 m diameter, top ~14-14.5 m, in the middle of a ~10 x 10 m square paver deck (roof_membrane) with a perimeter railing; the deck is drawn as a lighter square in ortho_2023aug.

The spine's NE face continues straight behind the one-storey annexes (W26-W29) and north of them; it is not a documented wall. It has the same column system as W25 (stair slot at the north end too, sv_W27 right) - use W25/W1.

Gap W13.b (1111.3,161.0) -> W14.a (1115.1,161.5), 3.8 m facing SE, is the glazed stair link between spine and east block: blue-tinted glass in a dark grid of ~3 x 7 panes from ~4 m to roof, brick below (sv_W14_TcGD, earth_corner_7). Draw it as curtain glass, window_glass with penthouse_metal mullions.

W16/W17 are the two sides of the bridge to E2 over the service lane (open at grade, lane passes under at ~4.3 m clear). The gap W16.b -> W17.a (2.8 m) is where it lands on E2 (E2 W3). The lidar footprint counts it as building; the ground under it must stay open.
W0 stands 1-2 m south of EIT W8: treat as a party wall; only the annex end (s 0-14) is visible from the lane.
The pavilion (W4-W6) is joined to the wing by the 3.3 m link (W3/W7); its roof is a separate flat roof at 5.0 m with a parapet.
The east block (W14-W19) is a later addition in a different brick and metal siding; it is in PHY's footprint but looks unlike the 1960s parts.

W0.summary: north end, almost entirely hidden: s 0-14 is the north face of the one-storey service annex (2.8 m, brick, black coping); s 14-36 is the spine's 11.6 m north end standing 1-2 m from EIT's south wall (EIT W8), effectively a party wall
attached: EIT (W8) 1-2 m north along s 14-36; the lane passes the annex end at s 0-14
W0.notes: Only seen edge-on: sv_W0_sZ3h/zcl (Sep 2014) look south down the lane past it; EIT facades.json notes 'a low 1-storey buff-brown brick link building with louvres and a black coping' in front of its W8 = this annex. Lidar: s 0-14 2.8-3.0 m, s 14-36 11.5 m. Nothing to draw beyond blank brick.

W1.summary: the long 1960s spine front on the west lawn: 3 storeys of orange-tan buff brick, 22 tall window columns (each storey: navy-black spandrel panel under a two-pane window with a transom, silver frames), thin light precast string courses at each floor, dark metal coping
attached: wing W2/W10 leaves the spine at s 78.5 (south end of this wall)
low handrail/ramp at grade near s 6-10 (sv_W1_dJgp left edge) - probably a ground-floor door there (guess, not seen)
W1.notes: Window module from sv_W1_dJgp (Sep 2014, square-on): floor 3.9 m, column pitch 0.88 of a floor = ~3.5 m, opening 1.6 m wide; spandrel panel ~0.85 m (#222426 shaded, reads near-black navy); window glass with one mullion and a transom, silver frames; dark head strip at the top of ground and middle floor openings. Count: SV module gives 22 columns over 78.5 m; earth_orbit_045 counts ~19-20 visible (ends hidden), so 21-22, I used 22. Brick: SV sunlit reads #a37051 (orange), Earth #deb7a4 (warm cast); palette brick_buff_sun is ~7 Lab from the blend #c39a7c; the brick is noticeably more orange than B2/EIT buff. String courses #d7cabc (precast_cream). Coping: dark flashing #434752 (brick_slate).

W10.notes: Zoomed sv_W10_u_6M (Sep 2014): fin pitch measured 0.95-1.0 m against the 11.8 m height, fins ~0.3 m wide; rows from the same photo: canopy fascia 3.6-4.1 m (its soffit is a row of shallow scallops/folded vaults between the columns - draw as a flat white band if needed), floor-2 windows 4.9-6.8, brick spandrel 6.8-8.8, floor-3 windows 8.8-10.8, brick parapet to 11.8. Fins are listed as piers (s every 1.0 m, 0.3 wide, 0.6 proud, precast_cream) so the current code draws them; piers run full height, but the real fins stop at the canopy (z 4.1-11.3, see the 'fins' entry) - below 4.1 only the round columns every 3.7 m stand on the face line. Entrance location from earth_facade_1 (2024). Column pitch 3.7 m (same photo). The stair bay at the east end (earth_detail_1b grid of glass) is a guess at s 41-44.6.
